stations.title: Station 2: Flexbox Core: Wrapping & Justification
stations.desc: Align items in horizontal rows and handle line wrapping automatically!
stations.story:
🗂️ Flexbox Wrapping & Justification!

Let's master alignment using CSS Flexbox layout systems!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • display: flex;: Initializes flex display layout on parents.
  • flex-wrap: Sets row wrapping behavior when items exceed parents' width. Values: nowrap (stay in one line), wrap (wrap into multiple lines), and wrap-reverse.
  • justify-content: Horizontal alignments inside flex rows. Values: flex-start, flex-end, center, space-between, space-around, and space-evenly.
stations.simple: Flex-wrap is like text-wrapping. When you run out of room in a row, the next box drops to the next line!
stations.hint: Set flex styles on parents: display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between;.
stations.challenge: Style the parent class 'flex-container' to display as flex, wrap items, and justify them with space-between spaces!

stations.title: Station 3: Flexbox Directions & Alignments
stations.desc: Align items vertically and flip axis orientations from rows to columns!
stations.story:
↕️ Vertical Flex Alignments!

Let's master item directions and vertical centering using Flexbox properties!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • flex-direction: Sets main layout axis. Directions: row (horizontal line, default), row-reverse, column (stacked vertically), and column-reverse.
  • align-items: Vertical alignment along the cross-axis. Configurations: stretch (expands full height, default), flex-start (align to top), flex-end (align to bottom), and center (perfect vertical centering!).
stations.simple: When you set flex-direction to column, justify-content controls vertical alignment, and align-items controls horizontal alignment!
stations.challenge: Style the parent class 'column-container' to have vertical column direction and center items horizontally!

stations.title: Station 4: Bootstrap Layout Utilities
stations.desc: Speed up coding using pre-made classes for spacing, borders, and displays!
stations.story:
🛠️ Bootstrap Utility Power!

Let's master pre-styled utility classes in Bootstrap to handle margins, paddings, backgrounds, and display states without writing CSS!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Spacing shorthand: m- (margin), p- (padding), mt- (margin-top), pe- (padding-end/right) from 1 to 5. E.g. p-3 adds medium padding.
  • Borders: border, border-primary, rounded, and rounded-circle.
  • Text Utilities: text-center, text-primary (blue), text-danger (red), and text-white.
  • Display: d-block, d-inline, and d-inline-block.
stations.simple: Instead of writing padding: 15px; in CSS, you can just add the class p-3 to your element in Bootstrap. It's incredibly fast!
stations.hint: Link Bootstrap and apply helper classes: class="p-5 bg-dark text-white rounded text-center".
stations.challenge: Style a division in Bootstrap with a dark background, white text, 48px padding (p-5), centered text, and rounded corners!

stations.title: Station 5: Level 2 Session 1: Grid System Intro
stations.desc: Rely on structural Bootstrap containers, rows, and columns for grids!
stations.story:
🕸️ The Powerful 12-Column Grid!

Bootstrap layout works on a flexible 12-column grid. Let's learn how rows and cols divide space!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • .container: Sets center-aligned layout boundaries.
  • .row: Group container for columns (acts like a flex parent).
  • .col: Column block. Automatically divides row space evenly!
  • 12-Column Rule: You can specify size using classes like col-6 (takes half row) or col-4 (takes 1/3 row). Sum of columns in one row should equal 12!
stations.simple: Think of the row as a box that fits exactly 12 small books. A col-6 is a book that takes the space of 6 columns!
stations.hint: Set up a grid with columns: <div class="row"><div class="col-6">Half</div><div class="col-6">Half</div></div>.
stations.challenge: Create a Bootstrap layout row with two columns, each taking exactly half the screen (col-6)!

stations.title: Station 6: Responsive Screen Sizes & Columns
stations.desc: Make layouts responsive across different screens using breakpoint classes!
stations.story:
📱 Layouts that fit every device!

Let's master responsive grid sizing based on target screens (phones, tablets, and laptops)!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Five Sizing Breakpoints:
    • col- (Extra small phones).
    • col-sm- (Small tablet, >576px).
    • col-md- (Medium tablets, >768px).
    • col-lg- (Laptop screen, >992px).
    • col-xl- (Extra large screen, >1200px).
  • Responsiveness: Write mixed grid sizes like class="col-12 col-md-6" (takes full width on phone, but half on tablet!).
stations.simple: When you specify col-12 col-md-6, your columns automatically stack on top of each other on mobile phones, but sit side by side on desktop computers!
stations.challenge: Style three column divisions to take full width (col-12) on mobile, but take 1/3 of the width (col-md-4) on tablet screens!

stations.title: Station 9: Level 3 Session 1: JavaScript programming Core
stations.desc: Add script tags, load data variables, and write logs to the console!
stations.story:
🔀 Welcome to JavaScript!

JavaScript is the brain of a website! It brings static pages to life with math, animations, logic, and interactivity!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Where to write JS: Put code inside <script> tags (internal or external).
  • JS Syntax: Declare variables using var (or let/const).
  • Data Types: String ("text"), Number (12), and Boolean (true/false).
  • Output Methods:
    • console.log(value): Prints directly to the console debugger screen.
    • window.alert(value): Triggers a pop-up window notification.
    • document.getElementById().innerHTML: Changes text inside HTML tags!
stations.simple: HTML builds the skeleton, CSS paints the dress, but JS makes the website think and talk!
stations.hint: Write JS output: console.log('Hello from JS!'); or declare variable: var score = 100;.
stations.challenge: Write a script declaring a variable 'studentName' containing 'Rowan', and print 'Activated Session 9!' to the console!
stations.starter_code: JavaScript Basics

stations.title: Station 10: Level 3 Session 2: JS Operators & Conditionals
stations.desc: Compare values and run code selectively using IF-else and comparison operators!
stations.story:
🗂️ JS Logic & Decisions!

Let's master mathematical operators and make smart decisions using conditional statements!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Operators:
    • Arithmetic: +, -, *, /.
    • Assignment: =.
    • Comparison: == (equal), != (not equal), >, <, >=, <=.
  • Conditional Statements:
    • if (condition) { ... } else { ... }: Runs code depending on logic.
    • Nested-if & switch statements.
  • Logical Operators: && (AND), || (OR), and ! (NOT).
stations.simple: Conditionals are like road signs. If the light is green, drive. Else, stop!
stations.challenge: Write an IF-else statement checking if a score variable (set to 85) is greater than or equal to 50, and print 'Pass'!

stations.title: Station 11: Level 3 Session 3: JS Loops: For & While
stations.desc: Repeat block actions infinitely or conditionally using for, while, and do-while loops!
stations.story:
🔄 Repeat with Loops!

Let's master repeating operations in programming to save writing hundreds of redundant lines!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • for: Repeats code a set number of times. Contains starting counter, limit condition, and step increment (e.g. for (var i = 0; i < 5; i++)).
  • while: Repeats as long as a condition remains true.
  • do-while: Always runs the code block at least ONCE before checking the condition!
stations.simple: A loop is like running laps around a playground. You keep going until you complete your target count!
stations.hint: Write loop: for (var i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { console.log('Count ' + i); }.
stations.challenge: Write a `for` loop that prints numbers from 1 to 5 to the console!

stations.title: Station 12: Level 3 Session 4: JS Arrays & Elements
stations.desc: Group multiple elements into lists, pop, push, and loop arrays!
stations.story:
🗃️ Store Lists inside Arrays!

Let's learn how to organize multiple related variables inside a single data container called an **Array**!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Create: Declare lists using brackets, e.g. var fruits = ["Apple", "Banana"];.
  • Access: Access items using index numbers starting from 0 (e.g. fruits[0] is Apple).
  • length: Property returning the count of items in an array.
  • push(item): Adds a new item to the END of an array.
  • pop(): Removes the last item from an array.
  • Conversion: Convert arrays to a single string using methods.
stations.simple: Remember, computer indexing starts at 0, not 1! So the very first element of your array lives at index 0!
stations.challenge: Create an array called 'hobbies' with 'Coding' and 'Gaming', push 'Robotics' to it, and log the array to the console!

stations.title: Station 13: Level 4 Session 1: JS Functions & Event Calls
stations.desc: Write reusable code blocks using functions and triggers!
stations.story:
⚙️ Reusable Code blocks with Functions!

Let's master reusable code scripts. Declare them once, and call them anywhere using functions!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Built-in vs User-defined: JS has pre-made functions, but we can write our own!
  • Function Syntax: Defined using the keyword function name(params) { ... }.
  • Calling: Trigger functions directly in code or assign them to web element triggers (like button clicks!).
  • return: Outputs values back from function scripts.
  • .value: Read values typed inside input boxes!
stations.simple: A function is like a recipe. You write the recipe down once, and cook it whenever you are hungry by calling it!
stations.challenge: Create a function called 'sayHello' that prints 'Welcome Rowan!' to the console, and call it!

stations.title: Station 14: Level 4 Session 2: HTML DOM Selectors
stations.desc: Navigate HTML trees and select elements using IDs, classes, and tags!
stations.story:
🌴 The Document Object Model (DOM)!

The DOM represents your web page structure as a tree of objects. Let's learn how JavaScript selects tags to modify them!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • What is the DOM? The structured tree map of a web page loaded in browsers.
  • Accessing Selectors:
    • document.getElementById('id'): Selects a single tag by unique ID.
    • document.getElementsByClassName('class'): Selects lists of classes.
    • document.querySelector('selector'): Modern selector matching CSS syntax!
  • Accessing Core Objects: Instantly access structural parts like document.head, document.body, and document.title!
stations.simple: The querySelector works exactly like CSS selectors. Use a dot for class names and a hash for IDs!
stations.challenge: Select the heading with ID 'my-header' using DOM methods and log its innerHTML text to the console!
stations.starter_code: Megaminds Studio

stations.title: Station 15: Level 4 Session 3: DOM Style & Event Triggers
stations.desc: Modify HTML tags, inject custom CSS styles, and handle button clicks!
stations.story:
🪄 Modify Elements on Clicks!

Let's learn how JavaScript modifies elements and style colors dynamically in response to user actions!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • Modifying Styles: Change layout CSS directly using element.style.color = "blue"; or overwrite blocks with element.style.cssText.
  • Set Attributes: Change element states dynamically.
  • Interactive Events: Triggers code in response to user actions: onclick (mouse click), onchange (typing change), and onmouseover (hovering!).
stations.simple: When you assign element.style.backgroundColor, you are painting your website dynamically behind the scenes using code!
stations.hint: Set click event and modify style: btn.onclick = function() { text.style.color = 'red'; };.
stations.challenge: Style the paragraph text color to green when the button is clicked using the `onclick` DOM trigger!
stations.starter_code: Magic Text

stations.title: Station 16: Level 5 Session 1: Objects, BOM & Royal Hotel
stations.desc: Construct Objects, interact with Window sizes, Local Storage, and final project!
stations.story:
🏆 JS Objects, Browser Windows & Graduation!

Congratulations, Grand Master! Let's complete the final hotel template with JS animations, storage, and explore modern ES6 variables!

💡 Key Lessons:
  • JS Objects: Group property data and functional methods together, e.g. var room = { name: "Suite", price: 150 };.
  • BOM (Browser Object Model): Interact with window environments.
    • Window size: window.innerWidth & window.innerHeight.
    • Shorthand scrolling: window.scrollTo().
  • Local Storage: Save persistent data (localStorage.setItem()) and read it back (localStorage.getItem()) so user details survive browser page refreshes!
  • ES6 Variables: Upgrade from var to block scoped let and constant const variables.
stations.simple: Local Storage acts like a tiny drawer inside the browser. Put a note in it, and it will still be there tomorrow when you open the page!
stations.hint: Set up a key in storage: localStorage.setItem('username', 'Rowan');.
